html:
The Guaná are a small Indigenous people of the Paraguayan Chaco, living near the Paraguay River north of Concepción. They speak a language of the Enlhet-Enenlhet (Mascoian) family, related to that of the Enenlhet, and call themselves Kaskihá.

The name Guaná was also used by Spanish and Portuguese writers for other Chaco peoples, above all the Arawakan groups related to the Terena, so old records can be confusing. The Chaco peoples lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, and resisted European control into the 1800s. In the 1900s ranchers and tannin companies took most of their land, and the Chaco War of 1932 to 1935 was fought across the region. See Paraguay.
